title: RSA exponent identity modulo a prime
statement:
Let $p$ be a prime, and let $m$, $N$, and $c$ be natural numbers satisfying $N = 1 + c(p-1)$. Then
\[
m^{N} \equiv m \pmod{p};
\]
that is, $m^{N}$ and $m$ have the same image in $\bbz/p\bbz$. (The congruence holds for every $m$, including multiples of $p$.)
hypotheses_covered: m, N (the exponent ed), c are natural numbers
replaced:
Let $p$ be prime and $m, ed, c \in \bbn$ with $ed = 1 + c(p-1)$. Then $m^{ed} \equiv m$ in
$\bbz/p\bbz$, where both sides are the images of natural numbers.
